verdict.summary: VisionPsy Standard Q8 (QVAC SDK) ranks first locally by 8 answers over VisionPsy Flash Q8 (QVAC SDK). No paired difference remains significant after Holm correction.
verdict.qualityConclusion: The observed rank order is not statistically decisive in this local run.
verdict.publicationSafeClaim: Independent local RealWorldQA corroboration on the public 765-question split, using a frozen upstream prompt/scorer revision and one QVAC-native runtime/backend: VisionPsy Standard Q8 (QVAC SDK) 446/765 (58.3%); VisionPsy Flash Q8 (QVAC SDK) 438/765 (57.3%); VisionPsy Flash Q4 imatrix (QVAC SDK) 428/765 (55.9%). The local rank order was not statistically decisive after paired Holm-corrected tests. This is not a claim of byte-for-byte replication of Tether's internal environment.

methodology.scoring: Exact multiple-choice option accuracy; one point per question; no cross-suite aggregation.
methodology.prompt:
Question: <question>
Options:
A. ...
Please select the correct answer from the options above.
methodology.providerOrder: cases deterministically shuffled; provider order uses a balanced three-position Latin rotation

scorerParity.implementation: Direct checksum-verified OpenCompass VLMEvalKit can_infer source execution

methodology.officialDifference: This run freezes the public VLMEvalKit prompt/scorer revision, dataset checksum, generation values, artifact hashes and QVAC-native stack. It cannot establish parity with unavailable vendor-internal environment details, hardware or numerical kernels.

officialWeaknesses.localFinding: Not directly measurable: RealWorldQA has no reliable label isolating price/plate OCR.

officialWeaknesses.claim: Correct chart reading but incorrect aggregation
officialWeaknesses.localFinding: Not directly measurable in this scene-heavy RealWorldQA slice.
Observed directionally: only 3 explicitly labelled left/right cases; Standard passed 1 and each Flash passed 2. The sample is too small for a conclusion.
Not observable under one-letter constrained decoding; all 2,295 answers were parseable.
Not isolated by RealWorldQA capability labels; requires OCRBench/DocVQA/InfoVQA or a dedicated high-resolution OCR slice.
Observed directionally but not decisively: Flash Q8 scored 438/765 and Flash Q4 scored 428/765. They disagreed on 76 cases (43 Q8-only wins, 33 Q4-only wins).

criticalities.title: Vendor-internal environment is not public
criticalities.risk: The public prompt and scorer can be frozen, but unavailable vendor hardware and full internal invocation cannot be reconstructed.
criticalities.solutionA: Call the result an exact reproduction.
criticalities.solutionB: Call it an independent local corroboration with a fully frozen local protocol.
criticalities.consequence: The local run is auditable without overstating vendor parity.

criticalities.title: Preprocessing differs intentionally between Standard and Flash
criticalities.risk: Standard consumes tiled/upscaled views while Flash consumes the native view; this is part of the model design but prevents attributing every difference to weights alone.
criticalities.solutionA: Keep official per-model preprocessing for product-realistic comparison.
criticalities.solutionB: Add a preprocessing ablation while retaining the official run as primary.
criticalities.consequence: Official preprocessing is the fair headline; the ablation explains whether tiling helps or hurts particular cases.

criticalities.title: Answer choices are imbalanced and category labels are heuristic
criticalities.risk: The majority answer letter is B (337/765); local capability labels are not an official RealWorldQA taxonomy.
criticalities.solutionB: Publish majority/random baselines and label every category breakdown as local heuristic analysis.
criticalities.consequence: This prevents category and letter-position artifacts from being mistaken for general visual skill.

criticalities.title: A single benchmark cannot validate all advertised capabilities
criticalities.risk: OCR, documents, charts, hallucination, instruction following and open-ended reasoning are weakly represented or absent.
criticalities.solutionA: Keep the claim strictly scoped to RealWorldQA.
criticalities.solutionB: Add official OCRBench, ChartQA, POPE and MM-IFEval replications later.
criticalities.consequence: The X post must not generalize this score to overall VisionPsy quality.

criticalities.title: Exact one-letter scoring masks answer quality
criticalities.risk: It measures option selection, not explanations, calibration, hallucination or repetition.
criticalities.solutionA: Use exact scoring because that is the benchmark metric.
criticalities.solutionB: Add a separate open-answer qualitative audit with a frozen rubric.
criticalities.recommended: A for benchmark; B as separate evidence
criticalities.consequence: Do not mix qualitative grades into the official accuracy denominator.

criticalities.title: The score gaps are statistically weak
criticalities.risk: The aggregate leader is only 8/765 answers ahead of the runner-up, and the minimum Holm-adjusted paired p-value is 0.5199.
criticalities.solutionB: Publish counts, confidence intervals and paired tests together.
criticalities.consequence: The defensible conclusion is “no clear local winner”, despite the rank order.

criticalities.title: System resource KPIs are not model-isolated
criticalities.risk: macOS GPU counters are system-wide and unified memory/process RSS does not fully represent model footprint.
criticalities.solutionA: Show them as live operational telemetry.
criticalities.solutionB: Label their scope and avoid cross-machine claims; use isolated device profiling for publication-grade memory data.
criticalities.consequence: Latency is reliable for this machine/run; GPU/RAM comparisons need narrower claims.

criticalities.title: Aggregate scores can hide different failure sets
criticalities.risk: Flash Q8 and Q4 differ by 10 correct answers but disagree on 76 individual questions.
criticalities.solutionB: Publish paired disagreement counts and inspect recurrent clusters.
criticalities.consequence: The Q4 result does not prove quantization is lossless on individual cases.

criticalities.title: Official-number provenance changes with precision and table revision
criticalities.risk: FP32/model-card headlines and matching GGUF rows are not interchangeable.
criticalities.solutionB: Compare each local file only against its matching GGUF column and record source URLs/date.
criticalities.consequence: This avoids claiming a gain or loss against the wrong precision.

criticalities.title: Repeatability is measured on a subset
criticalities.risk: A deterministic 100-case subset was run three times: every provider had 100% exact-output agreement and 0.00 pp maximum accuracy swing.
criticalities.solutionA: Treat the deterministic full run as sufficient for this exact protocol.
criticalities.solutionB: Publish the separate stratified repeatability audit without presenting it as a confidence interval.
criticalities.consequence: This tests local implementation stability, not all prompts, seeds, hardware or stochastic settings.

criticalities.title: Execution remains sequential on one device
criticalities.risk: The seeded shuffle and Latin rotation balance positions, but thermal drift can still affect performance KPIs.
criticalities.solutionB: Publish order and temperature-independent quality separately from device-specific performance.
criticalities.consequence: Accuracy remains paired; latency is explicitly local-device evidence.

repeatability.interpretation: Repeat 1 is the frozen 765-case primary run. Repeats 2 and 3 are new local inferences over the same deterministic 100-case subset. Accuracy ranges and exact-output agreement measure local repeatability; they are not confidence intervals for all possible prompts or hardware.

sanityBaselines.note: These are sanity checks, not competing model scores.

categoryLabels.publicationRule: Never describe these labels as an official RealWorldQA taxonomy.

reproducibility.retryPolicy: up to three attempts for transport/runtime failure only; valid wrong answers are never retried
